title: Client POC orientation: technical plan and success metrics
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc is the working orientation and technical plan for the client-led POC with NovaApps (retail personalization). Goal is to validate a production inference pipeline on Redwood Dedicated with two key integrations: (1) realtime personalization endpoint (low-latency text generation) and (2) batch embedding export for downstream analytics. This write-up is intended for the Solutions Engineering engagement lead, the customer's ML platform engineer, and the SRE/infra contact.

Top-level objectives (what success looks like):
- Functional: Serve personalized text responses for 95% of synthetic user flows without functional errors for 72 hours of continuous load testing.
- Performance: Achieve p50 latency <= 80ms and p95 latency <= 250ms for 512-token generation on the Dedicated instance under target concurrency.
- Quality: Maintain top-line ranking quality (CTR proxy) within 5% of the customer baseline on the supplied prompt set.
- Cost predictability: Projected inference cost for steady-state production <= $0.40 per 1k tokens (model + infra) when using the recommended batching and cache settings.
- Observability & ops: Full end-to-end tracing and alerting configured (token-level cost, p95 latency, error rate) with dashboards and runbook for on-call.

POC scope and out-of-scope:
In scope:
- Deploying model variants (fp16 and int8-quant) to Redwood Dedicated test pool.
- Integrating the customer's event API for request/response flows and webhook-based delivery.
- Running a 72-hour soak test with synthetic traffic and a ramp test to 120 RPS sustained.
- Evaluating quality regression using the customer prompt test set (n=2,000).
- Configuring Redwood Console dashboards and an initial alerting playbook.

Out of scope:
- Full production migration of customer data stores or replacing their feature store.
- Custom model training or fine-tuning within the POC timeframe.
- Long-term retention policy changes beyond 30 days of logs.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail matrix):
- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 80ms AND p95 <= 250ms during the 72-hour soak at target concurrency -> PASS/FAIL.
- Error budget: total 5xx error rate < 0.25% during soak -> PASS/FAIL.
- Throughput: Able to sustain 120 RPS for at least one 1-hour window without autoscaler saturation -> PASS/FAIL.
- Quality: On the provided eval prompt set, average relevance score drop <= 5% vs. baseline -> PASS/FAIL. Baseline metrics will be captured on day 0.
- Cost estimate validated: actual average token cost within 20% of projection in test runs -> PASS/FAIL.
- Security/compliance: No PII transmitted to Redwood logs during the test (customer-configured redaction verified) -> PASS/FAIL.

Technical prerequisites (customer + Redwood):
Customer must provide:
- API credentials and test key with scoped permissions (non-production).
- Sample prompt set + baseline metric export (CSV or BigQuery) and a 2,000-example evaluation workbook.
- Network info for dedicated VPC peering (if using Private mode) or allowlisted IPs for the Dedicated test pool.
- Minimal sample of production traffic shape and a preferred SLO table (latency percentiles, concurrency).

Redwood will provide:
- Dedicated GPU pool provisioned (2x A10G equivalents) for the POC window.
- A prebuilt deployment recipe and deployment script in the poc-scripts repo.
- Console dashboard template and an initial alerting runbook.

Configuration and test plan highlights:
1) Model variants and runtime config:
   - Variant A: fp16 optimized, balanced kernel selection, dynamic batching enabled (batch window = 12ms).
   - Variant B: int8 quantized using Redwood Optimize recommendations (quant profile q4_0), reduced memory footprint to enable higher concurrency.
2) Batching & cache settings:
   - Enable KV prefix caching for 80% of repeated prefixes (customer provides common queries).
   - Suggested batch size cap = 32 tokens for realtime; use load tests to validate.
3) Autoscaling policy:
   - Min nodes = 1, max nodes = 4; CPU/GPU utilization thresholds at 60/85%.
4) Observability:
   - Token-level cost telemetry enabled, trace ID propagation into customer's logs, and synthetic transactions for SLO measurement.

Milestones & timeline (3-week POC recommended):
- Week 0 (pre-PoC, up to 1 week): Agreement on success criteria, credentials, and baseline exports. Provision Dedicated pool.
- Week 1: Deploy Variant A, run functional tests, and workshop #1 (integration + wiring dashboards).
- Week 2: Deploy Variant B, run A/B quality tests against evaluation set, begin soak ramp.
- Week 3: Full 72-hour soak, cost analysis, runbook handoff, sign-off meeting.

Workshop agenda (Day 1 on-site or remote):
- 09:00 - 09:30: Introductions, objectives, and success criteria alignment.
- 09:30 - 10:30: Architecture walkthrough (Redwood Dedicated, VPC, routing).
- 10:30 - 12:00: Hands-on: deploy Variant A from poc-scripts and validate with curl tests.
- 12:00 - 13:00: Lunch / async Q&A.
- 13:00 - 15:00: Integrate customer request/response endpoint; small end-to-end demo.
- 15:00 - 16:30: Set up Console dashboards and test alert firing.
- 16:30 - 17:00: Next steps and action items.

Day 2 (optional - deep dive):
- Quantization playbook: hands-on converting a provided checkpoint to int8 and redeploying.
- Load testing clinic: run ramp scripts, inspect traces, and tune batch/window settings.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Redwood SE lead (Maya Chen): POC orchestration, deployment oversight, success criteria owner.
- Customer ML platform (TBD): provide credentials, traffic samples, run customer-side integrations.
- Redwood SRE (Ethan Park): capacity provisioning, autoscale tuning, and incident response during soak.
- Product engineer (Ritu Singh): console dashboards and trace hooks.

Success verification & test harness:
- Use poc-scripts/load-test-v2 to generate synthetic traffic (config files stored in the GitHub link above).
- Capture p50/p95 latency and token counts via Console and export to a CSV nightly.
- Run the evaluation harness (python eval_harness.py) against the 2,000-example set; produce a relevance/accuracy report and compare to baseline.

Risk register & mitigations:
- Risk: Quantized model shows >10% quality degradation. Mitigation: fallback policy to Variant A + run ablation on quantization settings; allow small tuning window.
- Risk: Network peering delays cause p95 spikes. Mitigation: enable regional routing and run localized synthetic tests; add warmup traffic.
- Risk: Unexpected autoscaler thrash during ramp. Mitigation: apply conservative scale-up thresholds and manual override during ramp windows.

Post-POC handoff deliverables:
- Final results pack: p50/p95 charts, error rates, cost breakdown, and quality comparison vs baseline.
- Deployment recipe and runbook in GitHub (PR linked above).
- List of recommended production configs and an optional annual cost estimate for Dedicated capacity.

Sign-off criteria and next steps:
- After the 72-hour soak, the joint team reviews metrics against the acceptance matrix. If >=5 acceptance criteria pass and no critical security gaps remain, customer signs an MOU to proceed to staging.
- Action items before sign-off: confirm redaction rules, finalize autoscale policy, and create ticket for production rollout plan (JIRA SE-7910).

Notes and open questions (to resolve in the kickoff meeting):
- Confirm the customer baseline measurement process and ownership for collecting CTR proxy.
- Decide whether to test Private (VPC) or Dedicated with allowlist for this POC. Private adds ~1 week to timeline for networking.
- Customer to confirm test window dates and on-call coverage for soak.

Quick links and artifacts referenced during the POC:
- POC scripts and deployment recipes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-scripts/pull/87
- Evaluation workbook (customer-supplied): shared via secure link during pre-PoC phase.
- Runbook template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/POC+Onramp+Toolkit

This doc is intentionally pragmatic and action-oriented. Use it as the single source-of-truth for the first POC sprint; update the action items section after the kickoff and capture decisions inline.
